title: Shortwave priority response lanes - playpen
content:
Context / one-liner:
This is a scratchpad for "Shortwave" — an experiment/PRD seed to support per-request dynamic priority lanes for responses. The goal: let applications opt into faster, higher-cost lanes or cheaper, slower lanes at request time (or via customer-level policies) while preserving an easy developer UX and predictable unit economics.

Why:
- Customers repeatedly ask for stronger SLAs per request (urgent vs background) and a way to trade latency for cost without creating duplicate endpoints.
- We already have routing and fallback plumbing; this is a lightweight surface to expose QoS tiers and integrate with batching/eviction/caching.

Core idea / MVP scope (rough):
1) API surface: client can pass header/query param: priority: {"shortwave", "standard", "economy"} or numeric priority 0-100. Default = standard.
2) Server semantics: shortwave -> prioritized scheduling, smaller batch windows, preferential kernel assignment when contended. economy -> delayed scheduling, larger batches, optional higher quantization.
3) Billing: per-token multiplier or a small priority surcharge; or map tiers to different unit prices. Must be transparent in response metadata (billing_rate, lane).
4) SLOs: shortwave target p50 latency X ms, standard baseline, economy best-effort with cost savings goal.
5) Safety: economy lane should not reduce model safety or hallucination checks; only transform scheduling/quantization.

User stories (sketch):
- As a mobile app engineer, I want to tag chat messages as "urgent" so they get routed to shortwave and users see faster replies during live sessions.
- As a marketplace operator, I want background indexing jobs to use economy lane to save cost while keeping eventual completion.
- As a platform admin, I want per-tenant default lane and the ability to whitelist endpoints for shortwave.

Acceptance criteria (for MVP):
- API accepts priority param; accepted values documented; invalid values default to standard and emit warning.
- Metrics emitted: lane, queue_time, batch_size, billing_rate; surfaceable in Console metrics.
- Shortwave demonstrably reduces p95/p50 under contention in internal load test by >= 30% vs standard at <10% extra cost.
- Economy reduces per-token cost by >= 20% (measured in integration with Optimize suggestions).
- No change to model outputs quality in shortwave vs standard beyond negligible variance (run eval on curated prompt set).

Design / runtime implications (brainstorm):
- Scheduler: need a fast-path queue weight for shortwave; preemptive scheduling could be risky—prefer weighted priority where shortwave consumes from a reserved share and borrow when idle.
- Batching: shortwave should have smaller max batch wait (ms), economy can have longer wait to increase tokens/batch. Also, allow lane-aware continuous batching.
- Kernel selection: allow shortwave to prefer lower-latency kernels (FP16 / less quantization), economy to prefer heavier quantization profiles. Need profiler to ensure no quality regression.
- KV cache: replay semantics must be identical; cache eviction policies could be lane-aware to protect shortwave keys.
- Circuit breakers: if shortwave capacity exhausted, automatically fallback to standard (emit fallback_reason). Provide optional guarantee: fail closed vs fall back.

Instrumentation / metrics to add:
- lane.request_count, lane.p50_latency, lane.p95_latency, lane.avg_batch_size, lane.queue_time_ms, lane.fallback_count, lane.cost_multiplier, lane.quality_regressions (from eval hooks).
- Per-tenant counters and per-route aggregation.

UX surface in Console (notes):
- Per-route toggle to allow/deny shortwave and default lane.
- Live latency/cost dashboard filtered by lane.
- Billing preview: show estimated cost delta if X% requests switch to shortwave.
- Rollouts: canary shortwave to subset of users to watch regressions.

Rollout plan (rough):
1) Internal prototype: expose param in dev API, implement scheduler weights + small batch windows. Run microbench and synthetic traffic. (2 weeks)
2) Limited dogfood: enable for internal teams with quota; collect metrics and quality evals. (2–3 weeks)
3) Beta: surface in Console as opt-in for customers; add billing toggles. (4–6 weeks)
4) GA: metrics/alerts, docs, example SDK snippets, pricing guidance.

Experiment matrix / tests to run:
- Load tests with mixed lane ratios (5/20/75, 20/50/30 etc.) to quantify impact on latency and cost.
- Quality A/B: same prompts through shortwave vs standard at scale to detect drift.
- Cost model sensitivity: test different pricing strategies (multiplier vs absolute surcharge) and analyze predictability.

Open questions / risks:
- Can we guarantee shortwave with hard latency SLOs or only probabilistic improvements? (legal/SLA implications)
- How to price without surprising customers? Need billing previews and alerts.
- Complexity in kernel scheduling and dedicated GPU reservation; might need to restrict shortwave to Dedicated pools initially.
- Might enable gaming (clients mark everything urgent). Need per-tenant quotas and abuse detection.

Implementation TODOs (personal checklist):
- [ ] Proto API param + SDK example (JS/Python).
- [ ] Scheduler prototype: weighted queues + per-lane batch windows.
- [ ] Metrics plumbing: lane labels everywhere.
- [ ] Billing hooks and cost preview UI sketch.
- [ ] Eval harness run: shortwave vs standard on core prompt set.
- [ ] Safety review: confirm no changes to model safety checks.
- [ ] Define default lane policies and admin controls.

Notes to self / heuristics:
- Keep surface minimal: single header + Console opt-in. Avoid adding new endpoints.
- Favor soft guarantees at launch; GA only after we have stable telemetry.
- Consider pairing with Optimize auto-suggestions: recommend lanes per-route when usage patterns fit.

Potential names considered: Shortwave, FastLane, PriorityLanes, Express. Shortwave feels compact and evocative — use it for now.

Quick sketches (developer notes):
- API: POST /v1/responses with body {prompt, ...} and header X-Redwood-Priority: shortwave|standard|economy
- Response includes headers: X-Redwood-Lane: shortwave, X-Redwood-Billing-Rate: 1.2
- Console: Route settings -> Default lane: standard; Allow lanes: [shortwave, economy] -> Quotas per-lane.

References / inspiration:
- Internal: turn-slab-economy notes (see JIRA-7083).
- External: cloud providers offering "priority" queues for compute jobs; networking QoS analogies.

Next steps (this week):
- Mock up API + SDK snippet for eng review (target: Fri).
- Ping Lena for scheduler prototype pairing.
- File a spike ticket for kernel selection costs (JIRA-7084).

Random scribbles / fallout ideas:
- "Priority credits" model where customers buy shortwave tokens that get consumed per-request; useful for predictable revenue and flexible throttling.
- Auto-shortwave: allow Redwood Optimize to recommend routes to auto-upgrade to shortwave for a short window during predicted peaks.

End of scratchpad.
